recipe.label: Cyanotype

traits.texture: quiet paper texture, pale botanical forms and subtly uneven blue print density
traits.composition: preserve garden depth and the tall conifer rhythm with a coherent blue/white hierarchy
traits.lighting: light appears as pale silhouettes and softly graded blue values

review_checks: foliage is structured rather than random silhouettes
limitations: This is an image aesthetic, not a real photographic exposure or calibrated cyanotype process.
Palette and fine geometry are prompt guidance and require visual review across a series.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: README style reference; intended use: One reviewed Cyanotype example for the Art Skill style catalog
Primary request: A lush sloping hillside garden with a thick foreground tree trunk on the left, tall slender conifers across the center-right, dense layered foliage, distant bluish hills, a small blue roof lower-center, external stairs at far left and a curving path on the right beneath a bright cloudy sky.
Style/medium: monochrome cyanotype-looking botanical landscape print
Color palette: #F1F0E7, #164B78, #2D6B98
Materials/textures: quiet paper texture, pale botanical forms and subtly uneven blue print density
Composition/framing: preserve garden depth and the tall conifer rhythm with a coherent blue/white hierarchy; Keep landscape orientation and the original broad framing; one image, no frame or panels
Lighting/mood: light appears as pale silhouettes and softly graded blue values
Requested output target: 1536x1024, opaque background, png; use only supported tool controls
Avoid: real people; copyrighted characters; logos and brand marks; copied artworks; unrequested lettering
Constraints: Keep the original layered garden viewpoint, left tree trunk, tall conifer rhythm, slope, distant hills and curving path. Simplify minor details only to suit the medium. Do not add a sea, island bay, rainbow or sunset.; No added people, brands, characters, captions or signatures; Use only this source photograph as the composition reference; never mix motifs from the other photos
